impact_summary: Reduces trial load when mediation succeeds, but certified judge-mediator scarcity strains daily caseloads.
Lower cost and preserved relationships when Akta Perdamaian is reached; non-attendance delays resolution.
Rp500M cap expands eligibility for commercial claims, but low legal literacy limits uptake without targeted outreach.
36,007 advocates registered by end-2020; enables remote filing and reduced travel costs.
Automates registers, but shortages of e-Court file administrators increase workload in regional courts.
Establishes non-discriminatory safeguards in line with CEDAW and SPPT-PKKTP, subject to regional judicial uptake.
Strengthens formal recognition of companions (pendamping) for women facing the law.
Integrates warrant, detention, and case-file exchange into SIP/e-Berpadu as registered institutional users.
Removes court-fee barriers (22,748 Prodeo cases in 2025) and provides free Posbakum legal drafting/consultation, with women comprising 67.8% (251/370) of users in the PA Purworejo empirical study.
Funds accredited Posbakum service providers via DIPA while shifting Prodeo eligibility screening from judicial putusan sela to Registrar/Court Chair administrative verification.
Provides procedural authority to summon, try, and convict corporate entities alongside managers (e.g., Putusan No. 3/Pid.Sus-TPK/2019/PN.Bgl), though Pasal 25 fault criteria remain non-binding.
Clarifies corporate representation and parent/subsidiary liability while exposing gaps in compliance-program defense criteria and fine-calculation formulas.
Provides binding procedural authority across civil, criminal, and TUN courts, clarifies 'serious threat' under Pasal 38(5), and operationalizes Anti-SLAPP screening.
Improves standing and citizen-lawsuit pathways, but delayed or unenforced civil restoration and compensation judgments limit practical remediation.
Enables collective resource pooling and equal compensation claims without individual lawsuits, though formal certification and public-notice costs create barriers.

Enables victim-centered restitution, conditional/supervision sentencing alternatives, and no detention extension during RJ peace efforts across 3,353 cases in 2025, subject to power-imbalance exclusions.
Establishes enforceable rights to Identifikasi Awal, Penilaian Personal, e-Court accessibility (Pasal 8), confidentiality and trauma-trigger protections (Pasal 10), and interpreter/companion oaths.
